# --instructions--

Store in the constant `pipe` an arrow function that collects any number of functions through a rest parameter and returns an arrow function which takes a value, applies every collected function in order (each one to the result of the previous) and returns the final result; with no functions, the value is returned unchanged

# --asserts--

`pipe((n) => n + 1, (n) => n * 2)(3)` must return `8`.

```javascript
tryCatch(pipe((n) => n + 1, (n) => n * 2)(3) === 8);
```

`pipe((n) => n * 2, (n) => n + 1)(3)` must return `7`, because the order matters.

```javascript
tryCatch(pipe((n) => n * 2, (n) => n + 1)(3) === 7);
```

`pipe()(5)` must return `5`.

```javascript
tryCatch(pipe()(5) === 5);
```

`pipe((s) => s.trim(), (s) => s.toUpperCase())("  hi ")` must return `"HI"`.

```javascript
tryCatch(pipe((s) => s.trim(), (s) => s.toUpperCase())("  hi ") === "HI");
```

`pipe` must be an arrow function that uses a rest parameter and returns a function.

```javascript
tryCatch(!/\bfunction\s*[(*]/.test(pipe.toString()) && /\.\.\.\w+/.test(pipe.toString()) && typeof pipe() === "function");
```

# --solutions--

```javascript
const pipe = (...fns) => (value) => fns.reduce((result, fn) => fn(result), value);
```
